subject.title: fix(models): add provider request rate limits

question: Should OpenClaw accept this narrow opt-in `models.providers.*.request.rateLimit` provider-dispatch config surface as the first core slice of outbound rate limiting?
rationale: The PR adds public config and runtime admission behavior while the canonical tracker still includes budgets, status/CLI UX, backoff, tool/channel scope, and persistence decisions that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Sponsor Provider Dispatch First
options.body: Accept the narrow model-provider request pacing surface after rebase and leave budgets, CLI/status, alerts, and non-provider calls as explicit follow-ups.

options.title: Broaden Design First
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers define a single outbound API governance design across providers, tools, budgets, status, and alerts.

options.title: Close This Slice
options.body: Close this PR and keep the broader work on the canonical issue until a maintainer-owned implementation is ready.

recommendation.title: Sponsor Provider Dispatch First
recommendation.body: Accept the narrow model-provider request pacing surface after rebase and leave budgets, CLI/status, alerts, and non-provider calls as explicit follow-ups.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the strongest adjacent provider egress history and product-scoping signal for the canonical rate-limit tracker.
